newsitem.title: USA: Dow stages strong comeback, ends modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: Dow stages strong comeback, ends modestly lower.

text.p: U.S. blue chips staged a strong comeback, selling off a further 75 points before bargain-hunters and Philip Morris buyers rescued the market to end well off session lows.

"The sell-off is over. We had an unbelievable comeback and buyers came out of the woodwork and back to the big cappers," said James Cramer of Cramer Co. "It's a mean-spirited tape that doesn't give you a chance for a bargain. You had to go in blindfolded at down 75 and buy. It was a limited two-day sale."
After falling 79 Tuesday, the Dow lost 20 to about 6423.
The Dow earlier skidded to a session-low 6367.41 amid skittish activity. Birinyi Associates Inc tracked four buy programs and three sell programs which had a net positive Dow impact of 18 points.
The Nasdaq Composite snapped its seven-session record streak, ending off three to about 1297.
Losers outpaced gainers 7-5 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 495 million shares.
Philip Morris rose two to 105-1/4 and gave the Dow a six point boost. Oppenheimer reiterated a buy rating on the stock. Another Dow component, J.P. Morgan rose 2-1/4 to 93-5/8.
Smaller cap stocks continued to outperform larger companies, with the Russell 2000 up fractionally to 358.

"It's part of the move from big cap names which have had such a dramatic move. People are positioning (themselves into) smaller cap names and we could get decent action going into them through January and February," said Jim Pizzo, senior investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

Weighing on stocks during the afternoon was news that Salomon cut the stock position in the balanced account to 45 percent from 50 percent, moving the five percent to cash. The allocation is now 20 percent cash, 35 percent bonds and 45 percent stocks.

"The market is trading at 19 times 1996 (S&P 500) earnings. The market has historically had trouble with a P/E above 18 times EPS. Also on a price/sales basis, valuations are the highest in history," Salomon's chief equity strategist David Shulman said.
"I see at best a sideways market next year or at worst down 10-15 percent. A correction, not a bear market. We had two wonderful years so we may have a pause," he said.
The long bond shed 13/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
The Federal Reserve's Beige Book report showed the U.S. economy kept growing at a moderate pace in November.
The report showed little or no sign of near-term wage and price pressures despite strong hiring and a tight labor market.

Drug, interest-rate sensitive stocks and select technology issues came under profit-taking pressure. IBM was off 1-3/8 to 161-3/4, Cisco Systems lost 2-1/4 to 63-1/4, Pfizer lost 1-1/2 to 83-7/8, Merck was off 1/4 to 80-3/4, Wells Fargo lost 4-1/4 to 275-1/4 and Freddie Mac was off 3-1/2 to 108-1/8.
Among individual issues, Continental Airlines class A rose two to 30-1/2 and Delta Air Lines rose 1/2 to 75-1/4. Both declined comment on reports they are in merger talks.
GT Interactive slumped 4-3/4 to 7-7/8 after warning fourth-quarter pre-tax income and revenues will fall short of Wall Street expectations. Lehman Brothers and UBS Securities downgraded the stock.
U.S. Robotics rose 3-1/8 to 76-7/8 after Hitachi PC Corp said it would use the modem maker's high-speed "x2" technology in its notebook computers. The shares lost 7-1/8 on Tuesday.

Flextronics slumped nine to 28-1/4 after news it expects to take charges and restructuring costs of $5-7 million and expects to be "modestly profitable" in the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 1997. Alex Brown cut the stock to buy.
CRA Managed Care surged 6-1/4 to 48-3/4. The company intends to withdraw plans to sell 500,000 company shares and 1.5 million shares by shareholders.

Forest Laboratories tumbled 9-1/4 to 29-1/2 after the company forecast operating losses for the next two quarters and for all of fiscal 1997. The company decided to eliminate trade incentives for all of its branded products to reduce high trade inventory levels, mostly of Aerobid, its flagship inhaled steroid product used in treating asthma.
Morgan Stanley downgraded Forest Labs.
Restaurant operator CKE Restaurants added 2-5/8 to 34-1/2.
CKE reported third-quarter share earnings rose to $0.28 from $0.16 a year ago.
Computer Science rose 2-7/8 to 79-3/4. The stock was named Merrill's Focus One stock of the week.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 3.35 to 1297.02.
The S&P 500 fell 3.18 to 745.10.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street Desk 212-859-1721
